text: The Patriots are in genuine trouble heading into Sunday's trip to Buffalo, with the offensive infrastructure crumbling around Drake Maye at an alarming pace: Greg Van Roten has been placed on injured reserve with a thigh injury, and the team signed rookie OL Da'Metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad in a desperate attempt to shore up the line. Maye himself has been brutally honest in the aftermath of Sunday's 35-6 demolition by Jacksonville, where he threw two interceptions and lost a fumble, calling his own performance and the offense's output "unacceptable"—and the numbers support his self-criticism, as New England sits dead last in the NFL with just 9.7 offensive points per game. The questions swirling around whether the Patriots are deploying Maye correctly are now competing with deeper concerns about the quarterback's early-season struggles and the structural collapse of an offense that looked promising in training camp, all coming together at precisely the wrong moment as the Bills loom at Highmark Stadium on Sunday at 1 PM ET.
